duplicate_check.notes: No Goldfinch or Goldfinch Prime canonical platform was found in the current repository review. A full candidate audit remains required before any promotion.

notes: The first-party governance proposal moves the legacy Goldfinch protocol into recovery-only maintenance mode and winds down Goldfinch Prime. A 7 July update states that Prime investors were fully redeemed, no new deposits are accepted, and the contract was paused, while legacy V1 borrower pools remain in payment or recovery. CYA focuses on CeFi and does not prioritize DeFi lending protocols in its initial scope, so this is staged for an explicit scope and entity-boundary decision rather than forced into canonical data. Review whether Goldfinch Prime should be modeled as a historically significant institutional-yield product/platform exception, whether legacy V1 and Prime remain one platform entity, and how customer outcomes should be scoped by product.

notes: BitMart announced an orderly wind-down on 26 July 2026. The notice schedules the end of spot, futures, and other trading on 26 August 2026 and formal trading-platform termination on 31 January 2027. It also states that BitMart Earn, Staking, Lending, Launchpad, and other products will be discontinued in phases, with dedicated redemption, settlement, and follow-up procedures to be communicated to affected users. Generic exchange Earn products are not prioritized in CYA, so BitMart is staged rather than promoted. Review whether the platform-wide shutdown and unresolved product-level customer outcomes justify a historically significant exchange-Earn exception, identify each affected yield or lending product, preserve product-specific custody and terms, and do not infer repayment completion before official settlement evidence is available.

major_event: Emergency platform suspension on 14 November 2022 after a failed liquidation process made part of customer assets unavailable, followed by migration, exit-payout and scheduled-release recovery programs, a reported release of more than 100 percent of fixed incident-date USD value for the scheduled-release cohort, and final platform wind-down on 30 June 2026

duplicate_check.notes: No canonical Inlock, INLOCK, Income Locker or inlock.io platform was found in the repository review. The automated candidate audit and direct canonical JSON inspection remain required before promotion.

notes: Inlock launched its custodial Savings Account in September 2020. On 14 November 2022 it suspended deposits, withdrawals, new loans, onboarding and interest after a failed liquidation process made a small part of customer assets unavailable. It later offered distinct recovery paths: migration to Vigiler, discounted early or exit payouts, and scheduled releases. In August 2024 Inlock reported that the scheduled-release cohort had received more than 103 percent of the fixed U.S.-dollar value of affected assets at the incident date. That metric is not a universal in-kind recovery rate: exit-payout users accepted discounts, migration users followed a different path, crypto-price changes affected asset value, and individual outcomes varied. The remaining platform was scheduled to wind down on 30 June 2026, with account-history and support windows continuing afterward. Canonical promotion must scope customer outcome by recovery path and avoid describing the incident-value milestone as identical full repayment for every customer.

major_event: Retail and professional digital-asset yield platform launched in 2021, changed yield rates in 2022, was acquired by XBTO in 2023 after regulatory approval, and transitioned toward institutional custody and trading under the XBTO group

duplicate_check.notes: No canonical Stablehouse, StableHouse or stablehouse.com platform was found in the repository review. The candidate audit must preserve the distinction between the historical yield products and the current XBTO custody and trading business.

notes: Stablehouse opened early access in November 2021 with digital-asset yield products and later advertised revised stablecoin and crypto rates. XBTO announced an agreement to acquire Stablehouse in August 2023 subject to Bermuda Monetary Authority approval. Current first-party Stablehouse and XBTO materials confirm that Stablehouse became part of XBTO and now operates within an institutional custody and trading group. This is an acquisition and product-transition record, not a platform collapse: no customer-loss, withdrawal-halt or repayment event is claimed. The acquisition announcement and current completion evidence do not provide one exact approval or completion date, so canonical promotion should use the announcement date for the acquisition event while leaving the exact completion date unresolved. Historical retail yield terms must not be replaced by current custody and trading terms.
